key_insight: GeoABC uses boundary geometry to make neural operators anisotropic near walls, better matching the different tangential and normal flow behaviors in aerodynamic simulation.
engineering_relevance: The method improves near-boundary pressure/flow prediction for airfoils and cars, which is critical for high-fidelity design optimization and CFD surrogate modeling.
method: Injects geometry-conditioned boundary correction into intermediate neural operator features
Treats tangential and normal directions differently to encode wall-constrained anisotropy
Acts as a plug-in module compatible with multiple neural operator backbones
evidence_signal: Across 2D airfoil and 3D car benchmarks, GeoABC reduced near-boundary relative L2 error by about 38% on average and narrowed the near-wall performance gap of mainstream neural operators.
watch_item: Performance gains may depend on accurate boundary geometry representation and careful integration into existing operator architectures.
paper_title: Geometry-Aware Anisotropic Boundary Correction for Aerodynamic Simulation
